newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds slip, underperform Europe.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds slip, underperform Europe.

text.p: Irish government bonds slipped into negative territory in active trade on Friday as a flurry of profit taking took a chunk out of prices, dealers said.

"It looks like Irish bonds are going to end the week on a poor note. Strong sterling in the foreign exchange market is making investors adjust their positions and take some cash from the market. We're underperforming the rest of Europe," one dealer said.
By 1520 GMT the eight percent bond due 2000 was 35p weaker at 106.85 to yield 5.94 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 was down 40p at 107.75 to yield 6.77 percent.

"The central bank's long term policy is insustainable and is not giving the markets any direction. Dublin is at 86 basis points over Germany in the 10-year spread which is not very encouraging. We've also underperformed U.K. gilts by four or five basis points," the dealer said.
CSO data showed on Friday that Irish producer output prices fell 0.2 percent in September and 0.7 percent year-on-year.
U.S. PPI inflation data rose a below-forecast 0.2 percent in September while retail sales data climbed 0.5 percent month-on-month.
"The U.S. data gave us a very mixed picture," the dealer said.
